From the moment of fertilization, cells are continuously growing, dying, and being replaced…
… this is achieved through the process of cell division. But before we get into too many details, we have some background info to talk about..

Each new cell, or 
daughter cell
,
 must contain the same genetic information as the original cell, or 
parent cell
 
DNA is this genetic information. It is found within the nucleus of each and every cell in the body.
parent cell:
Creating identical daughter cells is accomplished through the processes of DNA replication and cell division.

The best way to visualize chromosomes is a 
karyotype, 
which is an image of all the chromosomes the nucleus.

somatic cells
 (body cells, ie. not gametes) of humans

3

 or 46 chromosomes in total.

 and 1 pair of X

Homologous chromosomes 
are chromosomes with the same gene sequence as one another; one homologue is of maternal origin, and the other is of paternal origin.
Although homologues 
carry the same set of genes, they may carry different forms of the 
each 
gene (a
.k.a 
alleles
)
Because human cells carry to pairs of each chromosome, we are said to be 
diploid

Why is the Y-chromosome smaller?
The 
Y chromosome
 is smaller because it has lost many genes over time. It started as a pair with the X chromosome, but over millions of years, it stopped recombining with the X and many of its genes degraded. Now, it mainly carries a few genes essential for male traits, like the 
SRY
 gene for sex determination.

“Unpackaged” DNA is referred to as 
chromatin
:
DNA exists as c
hromatin during 
most of the cell’s life
 
but
 
condenses into chromosomes
 when the cell is about to divide.

Chromosomes
 contain very tightly wound DNA.

Before cell division, it is 
important for chromatin to condense into chromosomes in order to be able to separate them without damage and breakage. Image how hard it would be to separate cooked spaghetti that is all entangled!

Chromosome Number
varies from species to species…





More chromosomes DOES NOT necessarily 
result in
 higher intelligence or complexity

Humans = 46
Ferns = 1260
Dogs = 78
Bananas = 22

Human 
somatic (body) cells
 are 
diploid, or “2n”
This means there are two copies of each chromosome (one of maternal origin and one of paternal origin)
Human 
gametes
 are 
haploid, or “n”







2n = 46
n = 23

Some organisms, such as earthworms, contain more than two homologous chromosomes in each cell. These organisms are said to be 
polyploid
. 

Ploidy
Ploidy 
refers to the number of sets of chromosomes in a cell.

Duplicated Chromosomes
During the S-phase of interphase, DNA is replicated to double the genetic content of the cell. This is to ensure each 
daughter
 cell received a copy of each chromosome and the genes on it.  
We can observe this best when looking at 
unduplicated and duplicated chromosomes
.
The two arms of a duplicated chromosome are called 
sister chromatids
 and are exact copies of one another (result of S-phase)
Sister chromatids are held together by the 
centromere

Remember

The Cell Cycle
M-
phase
 accounts for the actual division of genetic information (
mitosis
) and splitting of the cytoplasm itself (
cytokinesis
)

If you were to look at a sample of healthy tissues under a microscope, most of the cells you would observe would likely be in interphase/early prophase
. 
Why
 do you think that is?
If cells spend most of their time (approx 90%) in interphase, the chance of finding a particular cell in interphase is much greater. Therefore most cells should be found in interphase at any time of observation. 

Actively growing tissues, such as the the tip of plant roots, however will have a slightly higher proportion of cells in mitosis
